module Knowledge
  class PublishDelivery
    def call(delivery_id:, store:)
      delivery = Delivery.find(delivery_id)
      payload = JSON.parse(delivery.payload)
      begin
        store.publish(id: delivery.event_id, type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload)
      rescue store.duplicate_error
        existing = store.read(delivery.event_id)
        raise 'conflicting event' unless existing == { type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload }

steps.message: The current job has two correctness gaps: it falls back to the stale snapshot when the authoritative row disappears or changes, and its `upsert` can replace a newer embedding revision. I’ll change the post-provider transaction to lock and validate the document by ID, then lock the document/version embedding row and only insert or update when the existing revision is not newer. This keeps provider execution outside the transaction and preserves tenant/publication/revision checks.

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      # The provider can be slow (and can perform its own database work), so do
      # not hold a database transaction open while it runs.
      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)

      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id)
        unless current && current.tenant_id == tenant_id && current.published? && current.revision == snapshot.revision
          raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
        end

        embedding = Embedding.lock.find_by(document_id: document_id, version: version)
        # A result for an older revision must never replace one which has
        # already been produced for a newer revision.
        if embedding.nil?
          Embedding.create!(document_id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                            version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector))
        elsif embedding.revision <= current.revision
          embedding.update!(tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision, vector: JSON.generate(vector))
        end
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

steps.message: The first regression run exposed a return-value bug in my implementation: `ActiveRecord::Rollback` is swallowed and the method still returned `:stored`. I’ll replace that control flow with an explicit acceptance flag, so invalid post-provider state returns `:discarded` while the transaction remains clean.

arguments.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='packs/knowledge/app/services/knowledge/embedding_job.rb'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id)
        unless current && current.tenant_id == tenant_id && current.published? && current.revision == snapshot.revision
          raise ActiveRecord::Rollback
        end

        embedding = Embedding.lock.find_by(document_id: document_id, version: version)", "      accepted = false
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id)
        next unless current && current.tenant_id == tenant_id && current.published? && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        accepted = true
        embedding = Embedding.lock.find_by(document_id: document_id, version: version)")
s=s.replace("      :stored
", "      accepted ? :stored : :discarded
")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
sed -n '1,160p' packs/knowledge/app/services/knowledge/embedding_job.rb
bundle exec ruby -Itest test/regression_test.rb && bundle exec ruby -Itest test/visible_test.rb

It looks like I’m testing the revision conditions effectively. I could also use the `published?` method to handle boolean checks. Full tests will need to be run as well.
